runs.text:
A tangled green bank,
birds calling from the bushes,
worms in the wet soil.

Each strange living form
tied to others, all shaped by
laws unseen but sure.

Growth begets more growth,
children carry parents' marks,
change creeps in with time.

Too many are born
for the earth to hold them all,
so the struggle starts.

The fit ones survive,
branching into new pathways,
weak forms fade to dust.

From hunger and war
the highest creatures arise—
death opens the door.

One breath, or a few,
started life so long ago,
simple and alone.

Earth turns round the sun,
bound by gravity's plain law,
while life keeps unfolding.

Endless shapes appear,
beautiful, strange, wondrous things,
still being born now.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
It is interesting to contemplate an entangled bank, clothed with many plants of many kinds, with birds singing on the bushes, with various insects flitting about, and with worms crawling through the damp earth, and to reflect that these elaborately constructed forms, so different from each other, and dependent on each other in so complex a manner, have all been produced by laws acting around us. These laws, taken in the largest sense, being Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance which is almost implied by reproduction; Variability from the indirect and direct action of the external conditions of life, and from use and disuse; a Ratio of Increase so high as to lead to a Struggle for Life, and as a consequence to Natural Selection, entailing Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms. Thus, from the war of nature, from famine and death, the most exalted object which we are capable of conceiving, namely, the production of the higher animals, directly follows. There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cycling on according to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
</passage>

runs.text:
A tangled bank grows,
birds singing, insects drifting,
worms in damp dark earth.

Different shapes, one web,
each life leaning on the next—
all born of plain law.

Growth begets more growth,
inheritance follows birth,
change from world and use.

Too many seeds fall,
so struggle sifts the living—
selection remains.

Forms split and diverge,
the weaker branches wither,
war without a sword.

From famine and death
the highest good yet emerges:
creatures raised in time.

Grand, this view of life—
one breath cast into few forms,
or maybe just one.

Earth wheels on through space,
bound by gravity's plain law,
while forms keep unfolding.

Simple start, vast bloom—
endless shapes both strange and fair,
still becoming now.

runs.text:
A tangled green bank,
birds calling from every bush,
worms in dark wet soil.

Each form intricate,
each leaning on the other—
all born of plain law.

Growth begets its kind,
traits passed down through quiet seed,
change from wind and use.

Too many are born,
so life wages war for room,
the fit ones outlast.

Branches spread apart,
weaker lines fade into dust—
this the struggle makes.

Out of famine, death,
something noble still emerges:
creatures raised up high.

There is a vast grace
in this—one breath, one beginning,
now countless bright forms.

While earth wheels through space
bound by gravity's plain pull,
new wonders unfold.

runs.text:
Tangled bank of green,
birds calling, insects drifting,
worms in the dark soil.

Each form intricate,
bound to countless others' lives,
born of quiet law.

Growth begets its like,
inheritance shapes the young,
change creeps through the flesh.

Numbers swell too fast,
life presses hard against life,
the fit ones remain.

Forms branch and diverge,
the weaker fade into dust,
new shapes take their place.

Out of famine, war,
death grinding on and on—
higher life emerges.

Grand thought to hold close:
one breath into early forms,
then endless unfolding.

Earth spins by fixed law,
around the sun, through the years,
while life keeps changing.

From simple beginning,
wonderful shapes still arise—
beauty still evolving.

runs.text:
A tangled green bank,
birds calling from every bush,
worms in the wet soil.

Each strange living form
depends upon its neighbor—
laws made this to be.

Growth begets its own,
traits passed down through generations,
change with every use.

Too many are born,
so life must struggle for life,
the weak fall away.

From this endless war,
from hunger and from dying,
higher things arise.

Grand thought: one breath given
to a few forms, or to one,
long ago in time.

Earth turns round the sun,
bound by gravity's plain law—
yet look what has grown.

From beginnings small,
shapes most wondrous and most fair
still unfold today.
